subject.title: Support Slack user-level events (events on behalf of users) for DM routing

question: Should OpenClaw support an explicit Slack user-account DM mode that receives user-authorized events and replies with the matching xoxp user token, or keep user tokens read-oriented?
rationale: The implementation is not just a routing fix; it changes Slack identity, token use, consent, and audit semantics for messages sent as a human user.

options.title: Design explicit opt-in mode
options.body: Add a named Slack user-account DM mode with authorization mapping, per-event send-token selection, docs, tests, and clear security warnings while preserving bot defaults.

options.title: Keep user tokens read-oriented
options.body: Document that OpenClaw intentionally does not operate as a regular Slack user and close or defer this request as unsupported.

options.title: Prototype behind maintainer gate
options.body: Allow a maintainer-sponsored experiment first, but do not ship it as general behavior until the security model is reviewed.

recommendation.title: Design explicit opt-in mode
recommendation.body: Add a named Slack user-account DM mode with authorization mapping, per-event send-token selection, docs, tests, and clear security warnings while preserving bot defaults.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete merged the original Slack user-token surface and is the clearest owner for the security/product boundary decision.
